answer: One defence is Proof of unique keeper bot execution log: executions logged by one keeper over hundreds of jobs, and the dune of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the cipher is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the walnut of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
